device.name: iBBQ / Inkbird BLE Meat Thermometer
device.notes:
BLE BBQ/meat thermometer with 2-6 temperature probes. Sold under Inkbird, Tenergy Solis, and generic iBBQ brands. $15-25.
PROTOCOL: uses custom BLE service 0xFFF0 with paired write/notify characteristics. Credential-based authentication is REQUIRED after connection — write a fixed 15-byte credential packet to 0xFFF2 before any other operation. Without this, the device ignores all subsequent commands.
CREDENTIAL: `[0x21, 0x07, 0x06, 0x05, 0x04, 0x03, 0x02, 0x01, 0xB8, 0x22, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00]` written to 0xFFF2. This is a FIXED value — not per-device. The "authentication" is essentially a magic wake-up sequence, not real security.
TEMPERATURE: uint16 LE per probe, in 0.1°C increments (divide by 10 for °C). num_probes = data_length / 2. Arrives as notifications on 0xFFF4 after enabling realtime mode. Treat the value as signed: probe-disconnect sentinel is 65526 (0xFFF6, int16 -10) on the GATT path (pybq; matches cloudbbq's -10 check) and 0xFFFF on the advertisement path (inkbird-ble).
PASSIVE BROADCAST (newer firmware): devices advertising as iBBQ-1 / iBBQ-2 / iBBQ-4 / iBBQ-6 broadcast all probe temperatures in BLE manufacturer data — signed int16 LE in 0.1°C starting at payload offset 10 of the manufacturer-data record — no GATT connection or credential needed for read-only monitoring. This is how Home Assistant core's inkbird integration reads the IBT-4XS (home-assistant/core#142370; library Bluetooth-Devices/inkbird-ble).
ENABLE REALTIME: write `[0x0B, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00]` to 0xFFF5. The device then streams temperature notifications on 0xFFF4 at a regular interval.
SETTINGS COMMANDS (all to 0xFFF5): - Celsius mode: `[0x02, 0x00, ...]` - Fahrenheit mode: `[0x02, 0x01, ...]` - Silence alarm: `[0x04, 0xFF, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00]` - Set target temp: `[0x01, probe#, low0, low1, high0, high1]`
  (probe# is 0-BASED — "probe-nr … from 0 onwards", uucidl gist)
- Battery request: `[0x08, 0x24, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00]`
BATTERY REPLY (on 0xFFF1 SettingsResult): header 0x24, then currentVoltage uint16 LE, maxVoltage uint16 LE. If maxVoltage == 0 use the default max — 6550 per the uucidl gist, 6580 per pybq (minor disagreement; treat the default as approximate).
CHARACTERISTICS: - 0xFFF1 SettingsResult (notify) — responses to settings writes - 0xFFF2 AccountAndVerify (write) — credential auth - 0xFFF3 HistoryData (notify) — historical temperature data - 0xFFF4 RealtimeData (notify) — live temperature stream - 0xFFF5 SettingsData (write) — configuration commands
DISCOVERY: advertised name "iBBQ" (newer firmware: "iBBQ-1/-2/-4/-6", which also broadcast temperatures in manufacturer data — see PASSIVE BROADCAST above), service UUID 0xFFF0.
VENDOR APP: Inkbird deprecated the BBQ GO / BBQ GO PRO apps (Dec 2022) in favor of the unified INKBIRD app; the BLE protocol is unchanged and was never officially documented.
CONFIDENCE: HIGH for all UUIDs, credential packet, enable realtime, temperature encoding, and settings commands — sourced from gist.github.com/uucidl (iBBQ protocol) and github.com/gleeds/cloudbbq.

credentials.notes: The 15-byte credential is a fixed magic sequence, not real auth.

factory_reset.effect: No credential state to clear beyond power-cycling.

methods.description: Connect, authenticate with fixed credential, enable CCCD on 0xFFF4, enable realtime on 0xFFF5.

steps.action: Scan for "iBBQ" name or 0xFFF0 service and connect.

setup.notes: Nothing to provision, but the connection sequence is not optional: after connecting, write the fixed 15-byte credential packet to 0xFFF2 before any other operation, or the device silently ignores everything that follows. Then enable realtime on 0xFFF5 to start receiving temperature data on 0xFFF4.

rejoin.notes: The fixed credential is a wake-up, not a bond. Any client can reconnect by sending the credential again.

entities.name: Temperature
entities.notes: Probe 1. The other probes are further fields of the same characteristic (probe_2_temp .. probe_6_temp); a consumer that wants one tile per probe reads them from the format block.

entities.name: Battery
entities.notes: Raw gauge value, not a percent: the reply carries the reading and its full-scale value as two fields and the percent is their ratio, which the entity vocabulary cannot express (see remaining_unknowns). No unit is claimed for the raw value. The reply only arrives after the battery request is written to 0xFFF5.

entities.name: Fahrenheit Display
entities.notes: Switches the DEVICE display unit; the BLE temperature stream stays 0.1°C either way. No unit read-back is documented, so the switch is write-only.

remaining_unknowns:
Battery percent is a ratio of two fields of the 0xFFF1 battery reply (battery_voltage_raw / battery_max_raw), and the entity vocabulary has no way to say "divide this field by that one" — so the Battery entity binds the raw reading and a consumer that wants a percent must do the division itself. The unit of the raw value (the open-source clients treat it as millivolt-like, full scale about 6550) has not been established.
0xFFF1 multiplexes every settings reply on one characteristic and the format block describes only the 0x24 battery reply; a consumer must check the first byte before decoding, because the schema has no frame-selector to say so for it.

characteristics.name: AccountAndVerify
characteristics.notes: CREDENTIAL AUTH (REQUIRED FIRST): write fixed 15-byte packet `[0x21, 0x07, 0x06, 0x05, 0x04, 0x03, 0x02, 0x01, 0xB8, 0x22, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00]` before any other operation.

set_target_temp.description: Set target temperature alarm for a probe. [0x01, probe_num, low_lo, low_hi, high_lo, high_hi] Temperatures as signed int16 in 0.1°C increments. probe_num is 0-based ("probe-nr … from 0 onwards", uucidl gist) — an earlier revision of this spec said 1-based.

characteristics.name: RealtimeData
characteristics.notes: Live temperature stream. Each notification is an array of uint16 LE values (one per probe), each in 0.1°C. num_probes = data_length/2. Enable notifications (CCCD) before enabling realtime. Probe-disconnect sentinel: 65526 (0xFFF6, i.e. int16 -10 — pybq, matching cloudbbq's -10 check); the advertisement path uses 0xFFFF instead (inkbird-ble). Treat values as signed. The layout below is what cloudbbq (app.js: a signed 16-bit LE read per probe, divided by 10, Celsius) and pybq implement; reported, not read back by this project. A notification is only as long as the unit has probes — two probes give 4 bytes — so the fields for probes the unit lacks are simply absent, not zero.

format.name: reply_type
format.notes: Only 0x24 is described here; other replies share the characteristic.

format.name: battery_voltage_raw
format.notes: Current battery reading in the device's own gauge units (the open-source clients treat it as millivolt-like but none states the unit). Divide by battery_max_raw for a fraction.

format.name: battery_max_raw
format.notes: Full-scale value for battery_voltage_raw; 0 means use the ~6550 default.

characteristics.name: SettingsResult
characteristics.notes: Responses to settings writes on 0xFFF5. Battery reply format: header 0x24, currentVoltage uint16 LE, maxVoltage uint16 LE — if maxVoltage == 0 fall back to the default max (6550 per uucidl gist, 6580 per pybq; approximate). The device also echoes the SilenceAlarm message here when the alarm is silenced via the device button. FRAME SELECTION: this characteristic carries every settings reply, not only the battery one, and the layout below describes the battery reply alone. Check byte 0 == 0x24 before trusting the voltage fields; any other first byte is a different reply (the silence-alarm echo, for one) and the offsets do not apply. The reading is a gauge ratio, not a voltage in any known unit: battery percent = battery_voltage_raw / battery_max_raw × 100, with battery_max_raw replaced by roughly 6550 when the device reports 0 (uucidl gist, pybq). Reported.

characteristics.name: HistoryData
characteristics.notes: Historical temperature data (if supported by model).
